content:
mira: Hey team — spotted a weird one in the Ruby sampleapp during onboarding. Token refresh seems to silently fail when background job triggers a request concurrently. Works fine in our JS SDK.

mira: Steps: start sampleapp, let background worker hit /embed every 30s, then rotate API key via env update. New requests keep 401s until app restart. No errors in logs except a failed retry.

tj: Can you paste the gem version and relevant middleware config?

mira: Using redwood-ruby 0.6.2 from sampleapp Gemfile. Middleware stack is Faraday default + our auth middleware:

```
class RedwoodAuth < Faraday::Middleware
  def call(env)
    env.request_headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{TokenStore.current}" 
    @app.call(env)
  end
end
```

mira: TokenStore updates when refresh happens but when two threads race the header isn't updated for the second thread.

oliver: Huh. Looks like TokenStore.current may be cached per-thread or mutated mid-flight. In Ruby concurrent requests in same process can overlap and the middleware reads stale value.

raj: We saw something similar in eng-ml with async batching. Short term: add a simple Mutex around TokenStore.current read/write. Longer term: switch to atomically reading from an immutable object (e.g., use Concurrent::Map or a frozen token string swap).

mira: Tried wrapping with Mutex on write, still saw occasional 401s. I think the race is between read and the update not the write itself.

oliver: Suggest double-checked locking pattern in the middleware to reload token from KMS if 401 and retry once. Also ensure the retry path doesn't requeue the auth refresh concurrently.

raj: I sketched a minimal fix in the gem — update the middleware to fetch token via a thread-safe accessor and add a single retry on 401: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ruby/pull/452 (WIP)

```
# pseudo
def call(env)
  env.request_headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{TokenStore.fetch}"
  response = @app.call(env)
  return response unless response.status == 401
  TokenStore.refresh_if_stale
  env.request_headers['Authorization'] = "Bearer #{TokenStore.fetch}"
  @app.call(env)
end
```

mira: That looks promising. I can add a unit test that simulates concurrent requests using threads.

tj: Please include regression test + changelog note. Also confirm behavior parity with JS SDK where we use a single refresh-in-progress promise to dedupe.

oliver: I'll review the PR tomorrow. If we want parity, maybe add a small in-memory promise-like object for Ruby (Concurrent::Promise) so refresh dedupes across threads.

mira: Great — I'll add tests and try Concurrent::Promise approach. Thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:

devex-bot: Reminder: link the PR to the 0.6.3 milestone and add reviewers @oliver @tj.
